text: A half step is the distance between two notes with no note in between. These are all half steps. Whole steps have one note in between. There's a note there, there's a note there, there's a note there, there's a note there, there's a note there, there's a note there, there's a note there, those are whole steps. At the top you can see all the different names of the black notes, and on the bottom is a diagram explaining whole steps and half steps. Now we're going to look at sharps and flats, this is where the black keys come in. A sharp is half a step above any note, so this is C and this is C sharp. This is F, this is F sharp, this is G, this is G sharp, actually this is E and F is actually E sharp because there's no note in between, but we don't use that too much. To find a flat it's one half step below, here's C sharp, now we're going to look at D flat, so C sharp and D flat are the same note, D sharp, E flat, D sharp and E flat are the same note, A sharp, A flat, G sharp is the same as A flat, B flat is the same as A sharp and so on, so all the sharps and flats are found by half steps.
